result.summary:
Wrote docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-025.md for WF02-REQ-025 (notification idempotency ledger, rate-limited sender, scheduled job runner) at branch feature/WF02-REQ-025, commit 80bca3a. Scope test: Step 2's artifacts_out (apps/bot/src/domain/notification.ts's new sendLedgeredNotification/NotificationKind/SendClassification/SendOutcome; apps/bot/src/scheduler/rateLimiter.ts's new createRateLimitedSender; apps/bot/src/scheduler/runner.ts's new startScheduledJobs; apps/bot/src/handlers/withdraw.ts's migrated sendPromotionNotification; apps/bot/src/domain/user.ts's getUserForNotificationById gaining broadcastOptIn; apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts's new notification_ledger table; a new drizzle migration) is real behavioral surface -- an at-most-once delivery guarantee backed by a real Postgres constraint, a real 429-backoff-retry sequence, and a real cross-process restart scenario. Full Steps 3b/4 apply.

Read docs/agents/instructions/core-directives.md, WF-02_requirement_implementation.md Step 3, docs/guides/qa_testing_guide.md, docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-024.md as the reference shape, docs/agents/design/REQ-025.md and REQ-025-schema.md in full, and the real implementations of sendLedgeredNotification (domain/notification.ts), createRateLimitedSender (scheduler/rateLimiter.ts), startScheduledJobs (scheduler/runner.ts), the migrated withdraw.ts, getUserForNotificationById (domain/user.ts), and the notificationLedger schema.ts definition -- so every case below is grounded in what is actually committed, not the design docs alone.

Independence finding, stated up front in the spec: BACKEND-DEV committed ZERO test files for this requirement's own new code (confirmed apps/bot/src/domain/notification.test.ts and apps/bot/src/scheduler/*.test.ts do not exist). The only pre-existing coverage touching this surface is incidental -- withdraw.test.ts's REQ-023-era 'REQ-023 AC6' and 'S10 rework' blocks (lines 321-464), written before REQ-025 existed, now exercising the migrated call path only because the call site underneath them was rewritten. Every case in this spec is therefore independently designed from scratch, not a re-pointing exercise.

All 6 stated ACs plus a new committed concurrency test have concrete, judgment-free verification cases:
- AC1: a genuine two-OS-process kill/restart test (scratch-verify-req025-p1.ts / -p2.ts, npx tsx, each opening its own fresh Pool/drizzle instance). The kill point is constructed precisely per design REQ-025.md 3.2's own instruction -- process 1 calls sendLedgeredNotification(...).then(() => process.exit(0)), so the kill happens strictly after sender.send() has already resolved (a durable file write completes before exit), never mid-flight. Process 2 opens a fresh pool/process and re-runs the identical call; pass requires p2's outcome is exactly skipped-already-sent, the delivery-log file has exactly one line, and exactly one notification_ledger row exists for the pair.
- AC2: a scoped git grep (new Set(|new Map( across domain/notification.ts, scheduler/rateLimiter.ts, scheduler/runner.ts, handlers/withdraw.ts only, to avoid false positives from unrelated codebase usage) confirming zero in-memory idempotency trackers, explicitly distinguishing rateLimiter's own sentAtMs array (rate-limit pacing state, not idempotency) from what AC2 actually tests -- PLUS a direct duplicate-insert SQL attempt against notification_ledger itself (bypassing the application code entirely), confirming the first insert succeeds, an identical second insert fails with Postgres 23505 naming constraint uq_notification_ledger_registration_kind, and a third insert with the same registration_id but a different kind succeeds (proving the constraint is genuinely composite, not accidentally unique on registration_id alone).
- AC3/AC4: a new committed Vitest file, apps/bot/src/domain/notification.test.ts, with all 5 cells of the S10 truth table as direct calls to sendLedgeredNotification (transactional+not-blocked=sent, transactional+blocked=skipped-blocked, marketing+opted-in+not-blocked=sent, marketing+opted-out=skipped-no-broadcast-opt-in, marketing+blocked-despite-opted-in=skipped-blocked -- this last cell specifically proves the blocked check runs BEFORE the classification branch, not merely that both checks independently refuse), plus AC3's own literal same-user/same-registration two-call case (transactional succeeds, marketing on the same opted-out user is skipped, both branches run). Per this run's explicit instruction, these call the function directly with classification: 'marketing' even though no production call site constructs one yet, to prove the API-level logic is correct and reachable code, not hypothetical.
- AC5: a structural grep confirming SendNotificationInput.classification has no '?' and no default anywhere in domain/notification.ts, plus confirmation the one real call site (withdraw.ts) supplies it explicitly.
- AC6: 3 cases in the same new file against a real grammY Bot with a stubbed api.config.use transformer -- retry-and-succeed (429 then 200, exactly 2 underlying sendMessage calls, sender.send resolves), retry-until-exhausted (always-429, rejects after exactly maxRetries attempts), and non-429-not-retried (403 rejects immediately at callCount===1) -- pinning down all three of design 5's stated behaviors, not only the happy path.
- Concurrent-call race, added per this run's explicit suggestion and committed as permanent regression coverage (REVIEWER/SECURITY-REVIEWER verified this ad hoc but never committed a test): two Promise.all'd concurrent calls to sendLedgeredNotification for the same (registrationId, kind), first at the same DB connection/pool granularity, second across two SEPARATE Pool instances (matching what SECURITY-REVIEWER's task-brief description says it traced ad hoc). Both require exactly one 'sent' + one 'skipped-already-sent' among the two outcomes, exactly one actual send, and exactly one ledger row -- named failure mode: a check-then-insert race (two statements instead of one atomic INSERT relying on the constraint) would let both calls read 'not yet sent' before either commits, producing a real double-delivery.
- REQ-023 regression: designed a case per this run's instruction even though it overlaps existing coverage -- re-running withdraw.test.ts's 'REQ-023 AC6' and 'S10 rework' describe blocks, with the overlap and its limits stated explicitly in the spec (proves the wiring/call-site migration, not sendLedgeredNotification's own logic in isolation, which AC3/AC4 already prove exhaustively; the existing fixture only ever exercises 2 of the 5 truth-table cells and never classification:'marketing' at all, since withdraw.ts always passes 'transactional').

Also added AC-schema (direct migration-file + schema.ts inspection of all 6 stated column/constraint facts, including confirming zero ALTER TABLE statements in the new migration) and AC-deps (git diff --stat on package.json, confirming REQ-025 -- unlike REQ-024 -- introduces no new dependency), per this project's established convention of covering mechanical claims beyond the numbered ACs.

Stated ISS-0014's --no-file-parallelism requirement in the spec's own execution-note section, with an added correctness note (not just an infra note) that AC1's two harness processes must run strictly sequentially -- p1 must have visibly exited before p2 starts -- since that sequencing is part of what the test is asserting, not incidental.

Gap found while reading: none beyond the zero-committed-tests gap this run's own instructions already named up front, which this spec closes in full. No design or implementation defect found -- nothing new to file under ISSUE_QUEUE.md from this step.
